title: Causal Learning for Trustworthy Recommender Systems: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying counterfactual inference approaches to achieve counterfactual fairness across sensitive attributes such as gender, age, and ethnicity in recommender systems.
Reviewing causal structure adjustment and counterfactual inference methods designed to reduce the unwarranted direct effect of an item's fame on recommendation outcomes.
Examining propensity reweighting techniques used to adjust for biased observations caused by users' tendencies to interact with top-ranked items regardless of actual relevance.
Reviewing counterfactual augmentation techniques meant to address unbalanced data distributions between highly active (heavy) users and casual users.
Surveying causal disentanglement methods that separate a user's genuine item interest from their intention to conform to overall item popularity.
Examining counterfactual reasoning frameworks that allow modifications to user embeddings to help users break out of isolated recommendation echo chambers.
Reviewing propensity reweighting tools to correct distortions in model training caused by Missing Not At Random (MNAR) interaction data.
